The deciding factor was the flat webpage composition with a rendered cursor and faux-tactile skeuomorphic UI (glass buttons, paper texture, metal seal) - it reads as a styled web/app design mockup rather than a photo, cinematic, or standalone product render. While the individual textures (metallic seal, glossy button) are rendered decently, their simplistic, template-like quality and the joke-copy web layout place it closest to a web 3D demo or low-budget app piece.

controls.collected: in round 7, for the first time: 5 fresh jurors who saw nothing else

rule: R2 passes when the judged share is no lower than the control share minus quality.jury.maxShareGap (0.2)
note: It passes by the rule: 0 of 20 on the judged pictures against 0 of 5 on the control, and the judged share is no lower than the control share less 0.2. What the rule does not see: no juror took any picture of the build for a photograph or a film frame, 19 of 20 chose (d) and one chose (c). The approved image drew the same letters, four (d) and one (c), and almost every juror of both gave the same reason: the picture is laid out as a web page with a pointer on it. So on this page the jury tells the build from the approved image by nothing. The fifth judged still of the unit, `marketing-foot`, is not in the jury: `quality.jury.stillsPerUnit` is 4, the key first and the rest in list order. All 25 jurors answered and none was replaced.
